clue.text: Playwright of former days breaking instrument put into the ground

indicators.note: one piece breaking another splits it open and sits inside it

parts.note: the harp is a stringed musical instrument
old describes things of former days
to inter is to bury, putting a body into the ground

explanation.surface: An old-time dramatist smashes a musical instrument and buries it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers both linked lights, 1 and 5 across; 'breaking' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The English dramatist behind The Birthday Party and The Caretaker, a Nobel laureate for literature.

clue.text: Bird has a weight at sea

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
taken as written
the Ross Sea is an inlet of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: A seabird is carrying something heavy out over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' reads as one phrase but splits in two: the word as written and the Antarctic sea named after James Clark Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge long-winged seabird of the southern oceans, a specific species of bird.

clue.text: I enter part of California State

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it
signals a run of letters taken from inside the next word

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone talks of moving into a region of California.
explanation.walkthrough: California is a red herring: the state wanted is its northern neighbour, and 'part of' takes a run from the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the Pacific coast, bordering California to the north.

clue.text: Unsaturated fats for man of stone

parts.note: something not saturated is dry
Fats Waller was an American jazz pianist and composer

explanation.surface: A dietary note about unsaturated fats, apparently meant for a stonemason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsaturated fats' looks like nutrition; it is DRY plus the jazzman Fats WALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who builds walls of stone without mortar, so a worker in stone.

clue.text: See 1
Growing buildings

definitions.meaning: a growing thing, a living organism such as a flower or shrub
the buildings and machinery of a factory or works

explanation.definitionFit: Both a living green organism and the premises and machinery of an industrial works.

clue.text: Student in new kind of surgery reportedly found body essential for growth

indicators.note: the student piece goes into the middle of the sound-alike
signals that what follows is a sound-alike of the spoken phrase

parts.note: new keyhole, a recent type of minimally invasive surgery
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A trainee in a novel surgical technique discovers what makes things grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns 'new keyhole' into the sound new-key-ole, written NUCEOLE; 'in' puts L inside after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant name for the nucleolus, the small body within a cell nucleus that makes ribosomes, needed for growth.

clue.text: Point to hole in Rumsfeld's stuff?

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A remark about a gap in the US defence secretary's material.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Rumsfeld, US defence secretary, notoriously said of looting in Baghdad that 'stuff happens'; stuff that happens is an occurrence.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumsfeld's 'stuff' is what happens, and a happening is an occurrence, the playful sense.

clue.text: Rumpus formerly tends to be by little brother

annotationWithheld.why: Rumpus formerly tends to be by little brother (7): BOBBERY = Rumpus formerly, but no parse of 'tends to be by little brother' gives BOBBERY that I can stand behind.
annotationWithheld.clue: Rumpus formerly tends to be by little brother

clue.text: Dishonest dolichocephalic Africans are utilitarians

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or dishonest
the Hamites, peoples of North and East Africa, were described in old anthropology as long-headed

explanation.surface: A description of crooked long-headed Africans who turn out to be philosophers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolichocephalic means long-headed; old ethnology classed the Hamites so.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Jeremy Bentham, founder of utilitarianism, so utilitarian philosophers.

clue.text: Country folk aiming for gold

definitions.meaning: the family in a long-running BBC radio soap about farming life
people shooting arrows at the gold centre of a target

explanation.definitionFit: The rural radio soap family, and bowmen whose target has a gold bullseye.

clue.text: German spy dancing around like an aesthete at a drinks do

indicators.note: the dancing letters go round the German word
letters that dance move into a new order

parts.note: Herr is German for Mister
an aesthete is arty, keen on art

explanation.surface: A German agent prances round like a dandy at a cocktail party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles the spy, and 'around' wraps those letters round the German title.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where sherry is served, a type of drinks party.

clue.text: Here's to our playwrights, changing to Athenian later

indicators.note: the letters change their order to form something new

explanation.surface: A toast to dramatists, switching to ancient Athenian theatre afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The national playhouse on London's South Bank that stages British playwrights' work, a cryptic definition by its function.

clue.text: See 22
Playwright has to change without a new plan

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatist has to make changes because his scheme lacks freshness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'new' rearranges the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The English television and stage dramatist from Hull who wrote The Beiderbecke Affair.

clue.text: NE as available at charity shop

parts.note: the letters N and E are most of the word new, missing its final letter

explanation.surface: The letters NE described as what a charity shop sells.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NE is 'new' missing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity shops sell second-hand goods in good condition, described as barely used.

clue.text: Re-director of entertainment on board

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act or spot
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A theatre director who reworks shows also handles the entertainment on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Re-director' gives it away: something that changes direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating platform for redirecting railway engines, or a record deck that spins.

clue.text: Painter of candied herb with a sex change

indicators.note: Latin and Italian -a endings are feminine and -o masculine, so A becomes O

parts.note: angelica stalks are candied for decorating cakes

explanation.surface: A painter of sweetened herbs who undergoes a sex change.
explanation.walkthrough: The feminine A ending becomes the masculine O.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico, the early Renaissance Florentine friar and artist.

clue.text: Old fashioned abuse of short course first in the haze

indicators.note: the course pieces go inside the haze

parts.note: mist is a haze

indicators.note: cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
A is first-rate, the top grade

explanation.surface: Ill-treatment of a brief course taken first, in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes ENTREE to ENTRE; with A it goes 'in' MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to ill-treat, so abuse in old-fashioned English.

clue.text: A little fall

definitions.meaning: a small quantity of liquid, as in just a tiny amount
to fall or descend, or a descent

explanation.definitionFit: Both a tiny quantity and a downward fall, two senses of one word.

clue.text: School fees include being on the wagon

indicators.note: one piece includes another by surrounding it

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone on the wagon, off alcohol

explanation.surface: The school's charges cover being teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: FETTES College is an Edinburgh independent school.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known private boarding school in Edinburgh, a specific instance of a school.

clue.text: The very thing for depression, a reader at the barrier

parts.note: just the ticket means the very thing
a col is a depression between mountain peaks
a lector is a reader in church or a university

explanation.surface: Something perfect for depression: a reader at the barricade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links; 'depression' looks like low mood but is the col, a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway official who checks passengers' passes at the station gate.

clue.text: Meeting runner and companion a breeze?

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour
air is a light breeze

explanation.surface: Running a meeting with a partner is easy, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting runner' is not an athlete but whoever presides.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a meeting or committee.

clue.text: Robin recently hatched

parts.note: a child is newly born, recently hatched
Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest

explanation.surface: A young robin just out of its egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is Robin Hood, not the bird; a robin newly hatched is in its youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly hatched robin is in the early stage of life, youth.

clue.text: Language was translated by Healey for reading aloud

indicators.note: letters translated are rendered into a new order
signals the name as spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Denis Healey, British Labour politician

explanation.surface: A language turned into English by Healey for a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' turns WAS into SWA; 'for reading aloud' makes Healey sound HILI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu lingua franca of East Africa, a language.

clue.text: In outstanding manner but without skill

definitions.meaning: in a remarkable or striking way
read as two words, not done with skill

explanation.definitionFit: Means in a remarkable way, and split as two words, not done well.

clue.text: Playwright takes common 1 across round North-Western river and Eastern river

indicators.note: the clipped name goes round the north letter
dropping the aitch is the stereotype of common speech

parts.note: the first name in 1 across
N is north
W is western
the Esk is a river in Scotland and England
E is eastern
R is river

explanation.surface: A dramatist takes a vulgar fellow-dramatist round two rivers in the north-west and east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' drops the H from 1 across, as in cockney speech; 'round' puts AROLD round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The English dramatist of the Wesker Trilogy and Chips with Everything.
